introduction.heading: Plumbing for Park City homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Park City were built in 1989 or later, and about 26% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Many of those homes are reaching the age when water heaters, faucets and fixtures need replacing. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Park City's Water Division draws from eight sources: three deep wells, a spring, two tunnels, Rockport Reservoir and water imported from the Jordanelle Special Service District, treated at the Quinns Junction, 3Kings and Spiro plants. Hardness ranged from 222 to 394 mg/L (13 to 23 grains per gallon) across the city's eight sampling areas, according to Park City's third-quarter 2026 water sampling. The U.S. Geological Survey classes that as very hard water. Hard water leaves mineral deposits in water heaters, faucets and appliances, and a water softener or filtration system cuts that buildup.

Park City says its water system is one of the most complex in the U.S., with 43 pressure zones, 16 pump stations and 49 pressure-reducing stations.
